title: Authentication Bypass via SQL Injection
impact: An attacker can bypass password verification and log in as the primary administrator (admin@juice-sh.op) without valid credentials. This grants full administrative privileges over the application and access to sensitive user data.
remediation: Use parameterized queries (prepared statements) or ORM bindings for all authentication database queries instead of string concatenation. Enforce strict input validation and apply the principle of least privilege to database accounts.

title: UNION-Based SQL Injection in Product Search
payload_used: ')) UNION SELECT id, email, password, '4', '5', '6', '7', '8', '9' FROM Users--
impact: An attacker can append arbitrary SQL queries to extract sensitive records from other database tables, such as user emails and password hashes. Exposing credential hashes enables offline password cracking and widespread account takeover.
remediation: Replace dynamic SQL string formatting in the product search handler with parameterized queries. Restrict database user read permissions so the search service can only access the Products table.

title: Reflected Cross-Site Scripting (DOM XSS) in Search Bar
impact: An attacker can craft a malicious search link that executes arbitrary JavaScript in a victim's browser session when clicked. This allows theft of session tokens (localStorage), unauthorized actions on behalf of the user, or phishing redirects.
remediation: Avoid using Angular's bypassSecurityTrustHtml() on untrusted query parameters and rely on Angular's built-in contextual auto-escaping. Implement a strong Content Security Policy (CSP) that blocks inline scripts and javascript: URIs.

title: Stored Cross-Site Scripting via Server-Side Filter Bypass
impact: An attacker can persistently store malicious HTML/JavaScript inside the database that automatically executes in the browser of every user who views the affected page. This compromises user sessions, exposes sensitive data, and enables worm-like propagation across accounts.
remediation: Apply multi-pass, context-aware server-side HTML sanitization using a vetted library (such as DOMPurify) rather than single-pass tag stripping. Encode all user-supplied content on output and enforce a strict Content Security Policy (CSP).
